identity.title: Resolved Millimeter-wavelength Observations of Debris Disks around Solar-type Stars

paper_type_evidence.quote: We combine our new observations with archival SMA and Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array (ALMA) data to enable a uniform analysis of the full five-object sample.

question.value: What are the radii, widths, grain properties and axisymmetry of the cold outer debris belts around five solar-type FEPS stars, derived with a uniform analysis of millimeter interferometry plus SED?

evidence.quote: We simultaneously model the broad-band photometric data and resolved millimeter visibilities to constrain the dust temperatures and disk morphologies, and perform an MCMC analysis to fit for basic structural parameters.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00470.S.
The disks were observed at 230 GHz (1.3 mm), and/or 345 GHz (0.87 mm).
For all observations, the correlator was configured to provide maximum sensitivity across the full 8 GHz available bandwidth.

arrays.value: SMA, CARMA (15 antennas), ALMA Cycle 0 (HD 107146 only)

evidence.quote: Each of the disks in this sample was observed with the Submillimeter Array (SMA).
The 1.3 mm wavelength ALMA continuum data on HD 107146 originate from Cycle 0 observations by (cite: Ricci15).
Our observations utilized the Subcompact, Compact, and Extended configurations of the SMA to sample baselines between 9 and 226 m

angular_resolution.value: as fine as 2.2" at 230 GHz and 0.6" at 345 GHz (SMA); ~2" overall

evidence.quote: to achieve an angular resolution as fine as 2.2” at 230 GHz and 0.6” at 345 GHz

observing_dates.value: SMA 2008-2012; ALMA 2012 Jan to 2013 Jan; CARMA Apr-Jun 2012

evidence.quote: The sources were observed for two to four nights between 2008 and 2012.

provided.value: Photometry and Kurucz photosphere models for SEDs

evidence.quote: drawn from the FEPS Legacy Survey archive

evidence.quote: one comparing the model disk SED to photometric data from the literature

evidence.quote: For HD 104860, the PA and $i$ were taken from (cite: Morales13)

what.value: PA and inclination of HD 61005 and HD 107146 from scattered light

evidence.quote: were adopted from scattered light observations of the disks (see (cite: Buenzli10) and (cite: Ardila04))
We assume that the grains are astronomical silicates (astrosilicates) with a bulk density of $2.7\, \text{g}\,\text{cm}^{-3}$ (cite: DraineLee84).

Mars and MWC349 were used to calibrate the flux

we approximate the grain emission efficiency following (cite: Williams04)

analysis_steps.goal: Fit disk centroids and initial fluxes

method.value: Elliptical Gaussian (elliptical ring for HD 107146) fit to continuum visibilities

evidence.quote: We calculated the centroid of the disk using an elliptical Gaussian (or, for HD 107146, an elliptical ring) fit to the continuum visibilities with the MIRIAD task `uvfit`.

validation.value: Offsets consistent with stellar position given proper motion

evidence.quote: All of the offset positions were consistent with the expected position of the star to within the uncertainties, taking into account the measured proper motion.

method.value: Literature values for HD 61005, HD 107146, HD 104860; grid search maximizing visibility amplitudes for HD 377 and HD 8907

evidence.quote: a grid search fit of PA and $i$ was used to maximize the visibility amplitudes
the results were consistent with the `uvfit` results

method.value: Kurucz-Lejeune photosphere + cold resolved disk + warm 100 K belt; modified blackbody with Q=1-exp(-(lambda0/lambda)^beta); model image sampled at data uv with uvmodel

evidence.quote: We then sample the model image at the same spatial frequencies as the data, using the MIRIAD command `uvmodel`.

key_parameters.value: p fixed to 0 except HD 107146; warm belt temperature fixed at 100 K; pixel size 1% of spatial scale of longest baseline

evidence.quote: we fix the temperature at 100 K and vary only the mass
The pixel size is set to be 1% of the spatial scale sampled by the longest baseline.

assumptions.value: Astrosilicate grains, density 2.7 g cm^-3, optically thin, radiative equilibrium

evidence.quote: We calculate the temperature of the grains by assuming that they are in radiative equilibrium with the central star and that the disk is optically thin.

validation.value: AIC used for warm belt significance

evidence.quote: We used the Akaike information criterion (AIC) to place a $3\sigma$ upper limit on the warm belt mass of HD 8907

method.value: Affine-invariant stretch-move MCMC on total chi2 = chi2_SED + chi2_VIS

evidence.quote: We add the chi-squared values for the SED and visibilities and use the total $\chi^2$ as the statistic for goodness-of-fit

key_parameters.value: 50 walkers, 5000 trials, burn-in a few hundred trials discarded

evidence.quote: We run 50 walkers through 5000 trials and discard trials for which the $\chi^2$ values have not yet converged

fitting.value: Uniform priors; a, M_D, M_B initialized in log space; R_in, beta (and p) linear

evidence.quote: We assume uniform priors for all variables.

validation.value: Best fit = lowest chi2 walker; 1 sigma from 68% of PDF; residual images in visibility domain

evidence.quote: The global best fit model is chosen from the MCMC walker position with the lowest $\chi^2$ value across the entire set of walkers and trials.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive grain size distribution slope and compare radii/blowout

method.value: q ≈ beta/beta_s + 3 with beta_s≈1.8; blowout size from radiation pressure formula; R_in/R_BB comparison

evidence.quote: Solving for $q$, we find that $q \approx (\beta/\beta_s) + 3$.

used_for.value: uvfit centroid fits and uvmodel model sampling

evidence.quote: fit to the continuum visibilities with the MIRIAD[^2] task `uvfit`

used_for.value: Similar affine-invariant sampler implemented (stretch moves only)

evidence.quote: We implement a sampler that utilizes only stretch moves, similar to the affine-invariant MCMC sampler, `emcee`, written in Python
The research made use of Astropy, a community-developed core Python package for Astronomy
We therefore derive a typical $q$ value of $3.5\pm 0.5$.
The median value was 42 AU, and all but one of the disks (HD 61005) was consistent with that median value to within the uncertainties.

findings_qualitative.value: All disks consistent with axisymmetric dust distributions within uncertainties; only a single 3-sigma residual peak in HD 107146

evidence.quote: There is a localized 3-sigma peak in the ALMA HD 107146 residual map

claims.hypothesis: Are the outer belts of solar-type stars scaled-up Kuiper Belts?
claims.experiment: Joint SED + visibility MCMC fit of five disks
claims.finding: Disks consistent with scaled-up Kuiper belts

evidence.quote: Overall, the five debris disks in our sample are consistent with scaled-up versions of the Solar system’s Kuiper belt.

claims.hypothesis: Do mm grains have sizes near blowout?
claims.experiment: Compared fitted characteristic grain sizes to blowout size
claims.finding: Grain sizes comparable to blowout size, consistent with collisional cascade (q~3.5)

evidence.quote: The $\beta$ values in our sample are therefore typical of what we expect of the grain size distribution in a disk undergoing a collisional cascade.

claims.hypothesis: Do the disks show non-axisymmetric structure?
claims.finding: No asymmetries detected within limited S/N

evidence.quote: We detect no asymmetries in the disks, to within the limits of our relatively low S/N ratio.

why_this_method.value: Simplified modified blackbody approach is computationally efficient enabling a full MCMC

evidence.quote: thereby allowing us to perform a robust statistical analysis of the data using an affine-invariant MCMC sampler

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: One vs two-component disk for HD 104860; two-component preferred

evidence.quote: We analyzed the SED and visibilities with one component as well as two, and find that a two-component disk best reproduces the thermal SED

limitations_admitted.value: Code is not entirely internally self-consistent; geometry of HD 377/8907 highly uncertain

evidence.quote: so the code is not entirely internally self-consistent
These geometric parameters are highly uncertain

referee_caveats_inferred: Disk widths mostly unresolved so p fixed to 0
Mixed use of AIC and BIC
Marginally resolved HD 377 and HD 8907 make geometry priors weak
Only one ALMA dataset, others lower-S/N

reproducibility.score_reason: Recipe is described but custom code, priors and reduction details are missing; only ALMA data demonstrably public.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Custom modeling code unavailable and ALMA is only one of several datasets.
